  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
  methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
  Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
  meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
  comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

  Watch the Meeting Online

  Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:
  City Council Meeting Videos
  Spectrum cable: Live streaming on Channel 3, Public Access Channel.

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – APRIL 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2022-23 Investment Policy. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for April 2023.

  D. AGREEMENT EXTENSION WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE
  SOCIETY (SGVHS) FOR ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 INCLUDING A NEW ANNUAL FEE AMOUNT OF
  $410,000

  The San Gabriel Valley Humane Society (SGVHS) has provided animal care and
  control services to the community for many decades. The City’s most recent
  agreement with SGVHS, approved by City Council on June 1, 2022 in the
  amount of $325,000, was an amendment to the agreement dated June 3, 2021,
  and has a term of one-year. With the existing amendment set to terminate on
  June 30, 2023, the SGVHS is requesting to continue services for the City for
  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 with the new compensation of $410,000. The cost to the
  City for SGVHS to provide a full-service animal care and control program for
  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 under the proposed extension would be $410,000. Based
  on prior years, the license fee revenue for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 is estimated at
  $35,000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to extend
  the existing agreement with the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society for Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 in the amount of $410,000 and approve the proposed revisions
  to the terms.

  E. ALL CITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES CONTRACT RENEWAL IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $173,664 FOR CROSSING GUARD SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2023-2024

  The City has had a Professional Services Agreement with All City Management
  Services, Incorporated to provide school crossing guard services since 2014.
  The most recent contract expires on June 30, 2023. Crossing Guard services are
  currently budgeted in the Police Department’s Contractual Services #121-751-
  00-22-000 in the amount of $130,752 for Fiscal Year 2022-2023. The fiscal
  impact for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 would be $173,664, an increase of $42,912.
  The new rates reflect the Los Angeles County price increases due to inflation.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a one-year Professional Services agreement with All City Management
  Services for crossing guard services for an annual amount not to exceed
  $173,664 and then re-evaluate their services and other opportunities for
  services in Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  F. SAN GABRIEL TOURISM AND MARKETING IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT
  (TMID) ANNUAL REPORT

  The San Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District (SGTMID),
  formed on February 5, 2019, is a benefit assessment district that creates a
  revenue source to help fund marketing and sales promotion efforts for San
  Gabriel lodging businesses through an increase in transient occupancy tax for
  the City of San Gabriel. The goal is to improve tourism and drive additional
  room night sales to assessed lodging businesses. The SGTMID includes lodging

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  4
   businesses with 100 rooms or more. Located within the boundaries of the City
  of San Gabriel; specifically, these lodging businesses are the Hilton Los
  Angeles/San Gabriel and the Sheraton Los Angeles San Gabriel hotels. The
  SGTMID has a five-year term, beginning July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2024.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept and file the San Gabriel Travel
  and Tourism Annual Report covering periods 2020-2023.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 23-25 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 100 BLOCK OF CRESTA AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Theodore G. Sams, a
  resident at 151 N. Cresta Avenue, for a temporary street closure. The purpose
  of this request is to hold a block party on Saturday, June 10, 2023, on the 100
  block of Cresta Avenue from 2:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-25 authorizing
  closure on Cresta Avenue between Las Tunas Drive and Hermosa Avenue from
  2:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Saturday, June 10, 2023.

  H. STREET BANNER REQUEST – HEALTH AND BEAUTY MEGA MIX EXPO

  The Public Works Department received a banner request from Alexis
  Salamanca, a representative of the Ofiso Community Foundation (“OCF”). The
  OCF will be hosting a Health & Beauty Mega Mix Expo on Thursday, July 27,
  2023, to serve the surrounding cities as well as the San Gabriel community. This
  event will be held at the San Gabriel Hilton Hotel. The OCF is requesting to hang
  one street banner at Las Tunas Dive and Del Mar Avenue and the other one at
  Las Tunas Drive and Bridge Street starting June 27, 2023, through July 28, 2023.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  5
   These locations have been verified and are available during these dates. There
  is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant the request, subject to
  compliance with Section 153.334(A) of the Municipal Code and the street
  banner conditions as listed on page 2 of the street banner application form.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NOS. 689 AND 690 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO INCLUSIONARY HOUSING AND
  DENSITY BONUS (ZTA23-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  On April 27, 2023, this matter was noticed for a City Council public hearing on
  May 16, 2023. Staff is requesting that this matter be continued to the June 20,
  2023 regular City Council meeting. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council open the public hearing and continue
  the item to the June 20, 2023 regular City Council meeting.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT
  WITH THE SAN GABRIEL HISTORICAL ASSOCIATION FOR THE HAYES
  HOUSE, HISTORICAL MUSEUM, AND JAIL

  The City of San Gabriel owns the property located at 546 West Broadway which
  is the site of Hayes House, San Gabriel Historical Museum, and Jail, which are
  operated and maintained by the San Gabriel Historical Association (SGHA)
  under a 2003 agreement that was renewed on July 21, 2020. The agreement

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  6
   allocates $1,500 per year to the SGHA in return for performing routine
  maintenance and opening the property to visitors throughout the year. The
  SGHA is requesting an amendment which would increase the annual cost to
  $3,000 and provide for a one-time payment of $25,000 to SGHA. If approved,
  an additional augmentation to the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 general fund budget
  will be added in the amount of $26,500, which includes a one-time expenditure
  of $25,000 as well as a $1,500 increase to the annual maintenance payment. In
  Fiscal Year 2023-2024, the general fund will contribute $28,000 for the upkeep
  and maintenance of the Hayes House, San Gabriel Historical Museum, and Jail.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to Property Maintenance Agreement with the
  San Gabriel Historical Association, allocating $3,000 annually towards the
  maintenance of structures; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the First Amendment to the Property
  Maintenance Agreement; and
  3. Direct staff to allocate $25,000 from Account No. 124-810-15-96-094 to be
  paid by San Gabriel Historical Association.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING USE OF ARTIFICIAL TURF OR SYNTHETIC GRASS
  ON CITY PARKWAYS

  Current State of California law encourages the use of drought tolerant
  landscaping, including artificial turf or synthetic grass on residential properties.
  Pursuant to the law, cities may adopt laws that provide standards for the type
  and installation of such materials, but may not adopt standards that would
  effectively preclude the use of such materials. State law is silent on the private
  installation of artificial turf on city property, such as a residential parkway.
  Currently, the City of San Gabriel’s Landscape Code only addresses the use of
  artificial or synthetic turf on private property but not within City owned
  parkways. There is no known fiscal impact for this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 16, 2023  7
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to amend the design
  standards for installation of artificial turf and/or synthetic grass by including a
  prohibition on the use of these materials in city-owned parkways.

  C. ACCEPTANCE OF GRANTS FROM ASSEMBLYMEMBER FONG’S OFFICE AND
  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENTS FROM ASIAN YOUTH CENTER AND FRIENDS
  OF LA LAGUNA

  The City was notified that it would be receiving targeted state funding on behalf
  of the Asian Youth Center and Friends of La Laguna. As the recipient and
  administrator of the funds, the City has developed, for Council’s consideration,
  agreements with the two organizations to ensure proper compliance with the
  requirements of the grant. There is no anticipated fiscal impact from the City’s
  participation in administration of the grant funds. The five percent retention will
  be sufficient to cover expected costs. The funds fronted for the friends of La
  Laguna project will be reimbursed by the grant.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Accept the Grants from Assemblymember Fong’s Office on behalf of Asian
  Youth Center and Friends of La Laguna.
  2. Approve the agreements with Asian Youth Center and Friends of La Laguna,
  as submitted.
  3. Authorize the City Manager to act as the authority on the City’s behalf in
  matters related to these transactions and execute any contracts with the
  state pertaining to the grant funding.
  4. Approve Resolution No. 23-29, required for the receipt of the grant with
  Friends of La Laguna.
